summary: You build an engine of production (steel, titanium, plants, energy, heat) across a long game, playing cards that combo off tags and thresholds while racing to push temperature, oxygen, and oceans to terraforming completion. It's a card-driven engine-builder with light multiplayer interaction — most of the game is optimizing your own tableau, with occasional greedy grabs for shared milestones/awards and tile-placement spite.
praised: Huge variety of project cards creating strong replayability and emergent combos
Satisfying long-arc engine building as production snowballs
Thematic tile placement on the Mars map
criticised: Long playtime, especially with 4-5 players or first-timers (can run well over 2 hours)
Significant luck in card draw/availability, especially in the corporate era draft
Downtime waiting for other players' turns
Some cards are much weaker than others, creating balance issues
Milestones/awards can be a race that rewards whoever gets there first with little counterplay

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with occasional tile blocking and awards/milestones racing

scoring.why: Final score comes from terraform rating, milestones, awards, greenery/city tiles, and card-specific victory points, so the winner is decided by whoever best balanced several scoring channels rather than maxing one.
